full_judgment:
11. Mr Rafiqul Islam Mehedi, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party opposes the Rule and submits that after marriage the plaintiff and defendant lad conjugal life, so the legal presumption would be that the marriage was consummated. He adds that after considering evidence on record the learned Judge of the Court of appeal below rightly decreed the suit as a whole, which calls for no interference by this Court. 

 14. On going to the materials on record it transpires that the marriage between the plain-tiff and defendant was solemnised on 16-4-1995. After marriage, the plaintiff was not taken to her conjugal home, however she was staying at her parents' house and lad conjugal life with defendant for about three/four months. Sometime after marriage the defendant went abroad for employment, and an returning back he divorced the plaintiff on 8-6-1999. It has been divulged from the evidence of plaintiff (PW 1) that on 16-4-1995 she was married with the defendant fixing the amount of dower for Taka 99,000 and she was staying at her parents' house wherein she led conjugal life with the defendant. The evidence of PW 1 furnished corroboration with the evidence of his uncle PW 2, Md Rahmatullah. On appraisal of the evidence of aforesaid witnesses, it transpires to me that the evidence of these PWs are consistent, uniform and corroborative with each other, particularly, in respect of leading conjugal life by both of them for about three/ four months. There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the consistent and corroborative evidence of those competent witnesses having no reason whatsoever to depose falsely against the defendant. The defendant however, cross examined them extensively, but nothing could be elicited to shake their credibility in any manner whatsoever. So, the same are invulnerable to the credibility. In view of such evidence it is legitimate presumption that the marriage between plaintiff and defendant was consummated in due course of leading conjugal life.
